defaultSelectionNotes: Source rules are scoped to the actual Application or System channel, never inferred from an Event ID alone.
All loaded IDs from direct IIS, ASP.NET, WAS and HTTP.sys providers are selected by default, including unreferenced IDs. An unknown ID is not evidence of an unrelated event.
Generic Windows providers use provider-specific ID defaults. Service Control Manager additionally requires an IIS-related service in the message.
These defaults are a troubleshooting starting point, not an exhaustive Windows event catalog or proof of IIS impact.

events.title: Application process crashed
events.meaning: Windows recorded an application fault. For IIS, confirm that the faulting application is w3wp.exe; this generic event is not proof by itself that IIS caused the crash.
likelyCauses: Unhandled application exception or native module fault.
The faulting module and exception code identify the next investigation path.
recommendedActions: Check the faulting application, module, exception code, and process ID in the raw event.
Correlate the timestamp with WAS 5011, .NET Runtime 1026, and IIS/HTTPERR evidence.
Capture a w3wp dump if the fault recurs and the event details do not identify the cause.

events.title: Windows Error Reporting record
events.meaning: Windows Error Reporting recorded or submitted diagnostic details. It commonly accompanies a crash, but is not itself the faulting event.
likelyCauses: An application or service fault generated a Windows Error Reporting record.
The report may include a bucket, report identifier, or dump location.
recommendedActions: Use the report identifier and event details to locate matching diagnostic data.
Correlate with Application Error 1000 and verify whether the affected process was w3wp.exe.

events.title: Application stopped responding
events.meaning: Windows recorded an application hang. Confirm the affected process and duration; a hang event alone does not establish an IIS root cause.
likelyCauses: A blocked request, deadlock, thread-pool starvation, or an external dependency that is not responding.
The process may be unresponsive without terminating.
recommendedActions: Check the application name, process ID, and hang details in the event message.
If the process is w3wp.exe, capture a hang dump while the issue is present and correlate with request evidence.

events.title: .NET process terminated by an unhandled exception
events.meaning: The .NET Runtime recorded an unhandled exception that terminated a process. In IIS, verify the process name and read the exception and stack details.
likelyCauses: An application exception escaped the request or background-processing path.
The exception may be the managed failure associated with Application Error 1000.
recommendedActions: Inspect the exception type, message, stack, application name, and process ID.
Correlate with Application Error 1000 and WAS 5011; use a dump when the event lacks enough context.

events.title: ASP.NET Web Event
events.meaning: ASP.NET emitted a Web Event. The event ID is a container for multiple ASP.NET event codes, so inspect the event code, message, application path, and exception rather than treating every 1309 as the same failure.
likelyCauses: An ASP.NET application exception, request failure, or configured health-monitoring event.
The specific event code and application details determine whether the event indicates user impact.
recommendedActions: Read the complete event message and identify the ASP.NET event code and application path.
Correlate errors with IIS requests and the matching application-pool events before changing configuration.

events.title: ASP.NET compilation error
events.meaning: ASP.NET reported a compilation error. The event message contains the compiler error and affected application context.
likelyCauses: Invalid or incompatible application code or assemblies.
The application-pool identity may lack required access to temporary compilation files.
recommendedActions: Use the full compiler message and file/line details to identify the failing assembly or source.
Check application-pool identity permissions on the specific temporary path named by the event; avoid broad permission changes.

events.title: IIS worker process could not load a module DLL
events.meaning: The IIS worker-process provider reports that a configured module DLL failed to load. The exact DLL path and error code in the event determine the cause.
likelyCauses: The DLL is missing, incompatible with the worker-process architecture, or has an unavailable dependency.
The application-pool identity or system configuration may not be able to read or initialize the module.
recommendedActions: Verify the named DLL exists, matches the worker-process bitness, and has its required dependencies.
Review the IIS module registration and the event's error code; repair the module installation rather than removing modules blindly.

events.title: Application pool disabled after repeated worker-process failures
events.meaning: WAS reports that the named application pool was automatically disabled after a series of failures in its worker processes. Read adjacent events to identify the underlying failures.
likelyCauses: Invalid application-pool identity credentials or a worker process that repeatedly exits.
Application initialization or a module failure.
recommendedActions: Verify the named pool's identity and credentials, then inspect nearby WAS and Application events.
Check whether the pool stopped through rapid-fail protection and diagnose the underlying worker-process error before restarting it.

events.title: Application-pool worker process terminated unexpectedly
events.meaning: WAS recorded an unexpected worker-process termination. The process exit code and pool name are key evidence; the event does not identify the underlying fault by itself.
likelyCauses: A process crash, unhandled exception, or worker-process startup/runtime failure.
A missing permission or dependency may also prevent a particular application-pool workload from operating.
recommendedActions: Correlate the process ID and timestamp with Application Error 1000, .NET Runtime 1026, and WAS 5011.
Inspect the exit code and collect a process dump if the termination repeats.

events.title: Worker process communication with WAS failed
events.meaning: Microsoft documents this warning as evidence of an IIS application-pool process crash or fatal communication failure between the worker process and WAS.
likelyCauses: The worker process terminated or became unable to communicate with WAS.
The event identifies when the process failure occurred, not necessarily the underlying code or module.
recommendedActions: Record the application-pool name, process ID, timestamp, and error code.
Correlate Application Error 1000 and .NET Runtime 1026; capture a w3wp dump if needed.

events.title: Application pool exceeded its shutdown time limit
events.meaning: The worker process did not shut down within the configured ShutdownTimeLimit and WAS forcibly stopped/recycled it.
likelyCauses: The configured shutdown limit is too low for in-flight work.
A request or application task is preventing the worker process from shutting down promptly.
recommendedActions: Correlate repeated events with recycling and user-visible impact before changing the limit.
Inspect long-running requests and capture a w3wp dump during a recurrence.

events.title: Related IIS service terminated unexpectedly
events.meaning: The Service Control Manager reports that the named service terminated unexpectedly. This reference applies only when the event message identifies an IIS-related service.
likelyCauses: The service process crashed or exited unexpectedly.
A dependent service, configuration, or resource problem may have stopped the service.
recommendedActions: Confirm the service name in the event message is WAS, W3SVC, IISADMIN, or another IIS-related service.
Correlate the failure and recovery events with WAS, Application, IIS, and HTTPERR evidence before restarting services.

events.title: Related IIS service terminated unexpectedly
events.meaning: The Service Control Manager reports an unexpected service termination. Confirm the service name; this generic event does not identify the underlying failure.
likelyCauses: The service process stopped unexpectedly or encountered a startup/runtime failure.
The cause may be recorded by the service itself or another provider near the same time.
recommendedActions: Verify the named service is part of the IIS request path before treating this as an IIS incident.
Check nearby WAS and Application events and inspect the service-specific error details.

events.title: Related IIS service state changed
events.meaning: The Service Control Manager reports that a service entered a running or stopped state. This is status evidence, not by itself proof of a fault.
likelyCauses: A service was started, stopped, or transitioned during normal operation.
An unexpected transition may follow a dependency failure, restart, or service crash.
recommendedActions: Check the service name and state in the event message and correlate the transition with user impact.
Use adjacent WAS, IIS, and Application events to determine whether the transition was expected.
